judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter concedes that "Grandfather" and "Grandmother" "have not always been interpreted and applied consistently" and then supplies a definition that is itself compound (the grandparent of the employee "or of his or her spouse at the time the grandparent dies"), leaving step- and in-law relations arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to state "The Times' interpretation" of Section 3-P of the preserved 1981-84 agreement (para. 12, c016), so whether a unilateral interpretive letter binds the Union turns on para. 14 (c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean prospective-only limitation keyed to "a death occurring prior to the date hereof"; the only softness is that the letter is undated ("July , 1988").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undated letter has to be located in time against the ratification-based effective date in para. 16 (c020), which is the only friction I found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quoted replacement first sentence is mangled and incomplete ("may elect to accumulate a ll ef hi ... leave days"), and the quotation of the deleted fifth sentence breaks off mid-clause at "for a later" — the amendment's actual content cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleting the liquidation-on-expiration sentence while allowing unlimited accumulation raises a question about what happens to banked leave at the end of the six-year term set by para. 1 (c001).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ertain neutrals subject to their availability and Willingness to serve" names no one and "effectuate the designation process" describes no mechanism — an agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 13 (c017) describes this Appendix E letter as concerning designations of "Status Quo" and Merits Arbitrators, categories the letter never mentions, and the arbitration machinery in para. 3 (c005) assumes a designated arbitrator exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]hall negotiate the conditions" is an obligation to bargain with no standard of outcome, and "when the normal daily order reaches 2500 copies" leaves "normal" and the measuring period undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the other negotiate-later clauses (c036, c037) and no provision elsewhere supplies the missing standard or a default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Performance is triggered by "satisfactory arrangements" and dated from "the date the revised Glen Burnie agreement has been put into effect" — an agreement not otherwise identified — and closes with the open-ended condition that the run "shall not involve The Times in increased costs."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The alternative plant designation ("Carlstadt or Edison") ties back to the Edison start-up provisions in para. 3 (c005) and to the further Lancaster clause (c037), which uses a different trigger for overlapping work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is conditioned on having "resolved satisfactorily any grievances, differences and disputes" and on the plant "running," then only requires The Times to "negotiate" arrangements that do not "involve The Times in increased costs" — every operative term is evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Glen Burnie/Lancaster clause (c036) covering the same magazine and plants under a different and earlier trigger, so the two sequencing regimes may collide.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare rate substitution from "6-1/2%" to "7.678%" that says nothing about the base to which the percentage applies, and characterises the new figure as merely reflecting "the present welfare contribution percentage."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The base is supplied, if at all, by 2(a) (c002) ("Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount") and is expressly cut back by Earnings Bonus para. 8 (c055), which forbids contributions on the bonus or on a deemed $25.93 increase — the central contribution question in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quotation marks are broken — `add "and an after tax deduction from wages of $3.67 after the words "per shift" in the first sentence` — so it cannot be told where the inserted text stops or where it goes, a mechanical error that changes the amended sentence's meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same $3.67 appears in 2(a) (c002) with a five-shift-per-week cap that this insertion omits, so the amended Section 13-H.1 and paragraph 2(a) may impose differently bounded obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first line of the schedule reads "3/31/87 = $.00 per shift" against a rising series ending at 14.00, so the 1987 figure is either missing or wrong on the face of the table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These casual contributions sit beside the percentage contribution in 13-H.1(a) (c038) and the per-shift deduction in 13-H.1(b) (c039), and para. 5(c) (c009) caps The Times' exposure to contributions "required by the Contract."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise insertion of "in writing, at least Sixty (60) days prior thereto" with "[balance as in original]"; the only softness is that the amended Section 9B text is not reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The very next amendment (c042) creates an excuse from the sixty-day requirement this clause inserts, so the two must be read as a unit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[R]egularly inserted in the Sunday or daily newspaper," "can demonstrate that it did not have sixty (60) days' notice itself" and "the promptest practicable notice" are all standards without boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the notice requirement just inserted by the preceding amendment (c041) while disclaiming any modification of "any other notice requirements pursuant to the Contract," leaving the relationship to other notice provisions preserved by para. 14 (c018) unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A] uniform portion of each employee's wage increase to become effective then or thereafter" does not say who fixes the portion, whether the Union may act unilaterally, or what a "vacation pay benefit" comprises.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Diverting wage increases interacts with 2(a)-(b) (c002, c003), on which "[p]ension and welfare contributions shall be made," and with Earnings Bonus para. 8 (c055) deeming wage scales increased by $25.93 — the contribution base could move as a result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ominal administrative costs" and "fully cooperate ... in developing any such alternatives" are unmeasured standards, and "alternatives" has no antecedent since the prior sentence speaks only of a vacation pay benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express condition on the diversion right in the preceding paragraph (c043) and echoes the no-increased-cost limits used elsewhere (c036, c037, c009), so it is consistent with the instrument's pattern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A commitment only to establish a study committee of two and two; there is no obligation whose scope could be disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Memorandum addresses terminally ill employees or committee procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is broken and incomplete — "it will guarantee all Saturday night Bulldog uding routes and relays)" — so the object of the guarantee (situations? shifts? jobs) is simply absent from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Bulldog" routes also appear in the returns clause of Appendix B (c028), and the guarantee interacts with the layoff protections in para. 3 (c005), but no direct contradiction is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]otwithstanding any provision to the contrary" is an unanchored override, and the exception for retroactive 1987 wages paid in 1988 is an exclusion whose boundary depends on how the retroactive payments in 2(a) are characterised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same 1987/1988 retroactive-wage exclusion is repeated in the gross wages definition (c050) and traces back to 2(a) (c002); the override language also cuts against para. 14's priority rule (c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed 3.86% of gross wages for five identified calendar years, with "gross wages" separately defined; nothing is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the definition in para. 4(a) (c050) and the payment deadline in para. 5 (c052) without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stub-period rate at the same 3.86%, expressed for a defined date range.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its payment timing is addressed both by para. 5's sixty days (c052) and para. 6's thirty days after 30 March 1993 (c053), which is a genuine, if narrow, mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tying "gross wages" to the W-2 "wages, tips and other compensation" box is objective, though the carve-outs make the figure something other than what the form actually reports.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sub-paragraph (b) (c051) adds back items that by definition never appear on the W-2, so the W-2-based definition is not self-executing, and para. 8 (c055) separately excludes the bonus from fund contribution bases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The add-back is confined to shifts for which Disability Plan benefits are received and only "to the extent that such State disability and workers' compensation benefits do not appear on the ... W-2" — precise, if fiddly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an express exception to the W-2 definition in para. 4(a) (c050) and dovetails with para. 8's wage-rate reporting for workers' compensation and state disability (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single deadline of sixty days after the end of "the applicable bonus period"; the only softness is that "bonus period" is defined only by implication from paras. 2 and 3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6 (c053) requires the January-March 1993 bonus to be paid within thirty days after 30 March 1993, and para. 7 (c054) uses sixty days from termination, so three deadlines govern overlapping payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]llocated in the manner set forth in Paragraph 7" points to a paragraph that confers a termination right rather than an allocation method, and it fixes obligations effective 31 March 1993, after the Contract term expires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The thirty-day deadline here differs from the sixty-day deadline in para. 5 (c052) for the same stub period, and para. 1 (c001) ends the Contract on 30 March 1993, making the post-term "$25.93 shall be added to the weekly wage scales" hard to place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is syntactically tangled — "to any fringe benefit provided under the contract or negotiated by any other union and the Times in connection with the current extension negotiations Or at any time through March 39, 1993" — with a plainly wrong date and an unclear reach of the trailing time phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 6 (c053) treats para. 7 as supplying an allocation "manner," and the right to pick up benefits "negotiated by any other union" duplicates the most-favoured-nation clause in para. 4 of the Memorandum (c006).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule covers "any benefit ... calculated on or determined by the employee's wage rate" with an illustrative-not-limiting list, then subtracts Welfare and Pension Fund contributions — a classic general-catch-all-against-carve-out structure, with "eliminate any duplication of the Earnings benefit or wage rate" left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its closing sentence directly opposes 2(a)'s "Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount" (c002) and the 7.678% rate amendment (c038), and it must also be squared with para. 5(c) (c009); this is the sharpest contribution-base conflict in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The number in the first sentence of Paragraph 3 is now eighty-eight (88)" identifies neither what the number counts nor which Paragraph 3, so the provision is unintelligible without the 1981-84 Memorandum of Understanding at pp. 103-5.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The referenced document survives only through para. 14 (c018) and was itself already changed by a January 1984 agreement, so tracing the amended text requires stacking three instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deleted sentence is identified only by description — "the sentence providing for certain floormen being available for driving assignments" — so which sentence is struck is a matter of construction if more than one fits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Removing floormen from driving assignments interacts with the additional floor situations and chauffeurs created in Appendix A (c021-c022), though no express contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states a practice as of a moment ("now 121" machines at three locations) while acknowledging that new machines have been folded into those locations, and the OCR-scrambled address list makes two of the three sites unreadable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This internal memorandum was transmitted as the definition of the "present practices" preserved by the Appendix B-1 side letter (c029), yet it covers only the West Side Direct area while that letter speaks of "The Times direct operation" generally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It puts "abolition" in quotation marks and then preserves everything in the abolished memorandum "other than that portion Providing for attrition of those routes" — a saving clause whose reach depends on what counts as the attrition portion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely qualifies the Appendix B statement that the 22 November 1983 Memorandum "shall be abolished" (c026), so one text says abolished and the other says mostly still in force, with para. 14 (c018) governing which prevails.
